Check that a cached Gmail token will be found without a browser

Source: R/mc_auth_check.R
mc_auth_check.Rd

Run before anything that sends without a person at the keyboard (Rscript, cron, CI). gargle finds a cached token partly by the name of the OAuth client it was minted under, and it computes that name afresh in every session. When the stored and computed names differ, non-interactive auth fails with gargle's generic "Can't get Google credentials", even though the token is still valid. mc_auth_check() compares the two names and, when they differ, says which they are and how to fix it.

Usage

mc_auth_check(email = default_from(), cache = NULL)

Arguments

email

Email address whose cached token to check. Default uses getOption("mc.from"), then the MC_FROM environment variable.

cache

Path to gargle's token cache. Default NULL uses the gargle_oauth_cache option, else gargle's default cache directory.

Value

TRUE, invisibly, when a cached token for email matches the session's OAuth client. Errors otherwise.

Details

The check is necessary, not sufficient. gargle's cache key also covers the scopes a token was granted, so a token whose client name matches but which was minted with narrower scopes than gmailr requests is still not found. Tokens for the same email minted by other Google packages, under other OAuth clients, are ignored.

The check is for the account named by email. A scheduled send that fires later authenticates through gmailr's own default, the GMAILR_EMAIL environment variable or the gargle_oauth_email option, and with neither set gargle takes the first matching cached token. Set GMAILR_EMAIL to the same address for unattended sends, so the token checked is the one used.

The check reads the context of the R process it runs in: its OAuth client, its cache option and the rlang it has loaded. Run it the way the send will run: from a fresh process started in your home directory (cd ~ && Rscript -e 'mc::mc_auth_check()'), because a launchd job starts in / and reads ~/.Renviron and ~/.Rprofile, never a project's. Keep GMAILR_OAUTH_CLIENT, GMAILR_EMAIL and MC_FROM in ~/.Renviron: a launchd job does not see variables exported from a shell profile.

Troubleshooting

Upgrading rlang invalidates the gargle token cache. gargle names the OAuth client <project_id>_<hash>, where the hash comes from rlang::hash(), and that function's output changed in rlang 1.3.0. A token minted under the older rlang carries the old name, so a session running the newer rlang does not find it. An interactive session hides this, because it offers the cached tokens rather than matching them strictly.

To fix it:

  1. Start a fresh R session, so the rlang loaded is the one installed. Re-authenticating from a session started before the upgrade writes the token under the old name again.

  2. Move the stale token file this function names out of the cache.

  3. Run mc_auth() and complete the browser flow.

  4. Run mc_auth_check() again from a non-interactive session, e.g. Rscript -e 'mc::mc_auth_check()'.

See also

mc_auth() to authenticate.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Before a scheduled or cron-driven send
mc_auth_check()

mc_auth_check("you@example.com")
} # }
